reading.body:
EdgeConneX DET01 sits in Oakland County, Michigan, with 39,900 square feet of published technical space. No IT load figure in megawatts is published on the operator's spec page, so no translation into racks or accelerators is possible from the data this site holds. The absence of a power figure is the single most important gap for any reader trying to assess AI hosting capacity here.

The four certifications qualify the campus to host regulated workloads: SOC 2 Type 2 addresses audited controls over security and availability, PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments, HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information, and ISO 27001 certifies a managed information-security framework. These credentials point toward compliance-sensitive enterprise workloads rather than toward the high-density, power-intensive GPU clusters that define frontier AI training. Which tenants or workload types are actually present is not published.

Michigan has six data center facilities mapped in this site's records, and none of the six, including DET01, publishes a megawatt figure, making the state's total published IT capacity zero by that measure. DET01 ranks first in the state by published megawatts only in the trivial sense that every facility in Michigan shares that rank at zero. Until an operator publishes a power figure, the campus cannot be placed on the capacity scale that matters most to AI infrastructure decisions.
